item.title: When Thai Heritage Becomes Something You Can Take Home
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
A new collaboration between Anantara Hotels & Resorts and Thai heritage silk house Jim Thompson brings the spirit of Thailand beyond the walls of the resort with Soul of Siam, an exclusive nine-piece collection of resort wear and travel accessories. Debuting September 1 across Anantara properties throughout Thailand, the collection translates the visual language of Thai culture into pieces designed to travel: a wrap kaftan, silk scarf, pocket square, beach bag, cap, vanity pouch and laptop cases, all featuring either the signature Soul of Siam print or a more understated deep navy palette.

The collection draws on imagery inspired by Thai temple architecture, mythical guardians, rural landscapes and tropical flora, while traditional silk-making techniques championed by Jim Thompson give the pieces a tangible connection to the country’s craft heritage. The collaboration builds on an existing relationship between the brands, including Jim Thompson-designed spaces at Anantara Siam Bangkok Hotel and Anantara Mai Khao Phuket Villas. Campaign imagery, photographed at Anantara Siam Bangkok and Anantara Riverside Bangkok, features Thai personalities Cindy Sirinya Bishop and Byron Bishop, adding a distinctly local face to the pairing of heritage and contemporary luxury.

The Curated Take:
The most interesting luxury souvenirs are the ones that don’t look like souvenirs. Soul of Siam takes something deeply rooted in Thai culture and turns it into something travelers can actually incorporate into their lives long after the resort stay ends. It also reflects a broader evolution in luxury hospitality, where the experience increasingly extends beyond the room itself and into design, fashion and objects with a sense of place. For travelers who want to bring a piece of Thailand home without resorting to the predictable, this collaboration makes the destination wearable.

Photo credit: © Anantara Hotels & Resorts / Jim Thompson

item.title: Vienna at Christmas, on Her Own Terms
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
What if the European Christmas trip you’ve always dreamed about didn’t have to wait for someone else’s calendar? That’s the idea behind Illuminare Retreat, where founder Amanda Donaho is seeing more women choose meaningful travel on their own rather than postpone it until a partner, friend or family member is available. Her intimate European retreats offer a middle ground between traditional group travel and going completely solo, giving women the freedom to travel independently with the ease, connection and thoughtful planning of a curated experience.

That approach takes on a particularly festive dimension this year with Illuminare’s inaugural Vienna Christmas Retreat, a week designed around the Austrian capital’s Christmas markets, historic cafés, cultural experiences and holiday traditions. The retreat speaks to a broader shift in how women are approaching solo travel, particularly among women in their 30s through 70s who are looking not only for independence, but also friendship, discovery and the opportunity to experience a destination on their own terms.

The Curated Take:
There’s something wonderfully liberating about refusing to put a dream trip on hold simply because the right travel companion hasn’t appeared on the calendar. Vienna at Christmas is already a compelling proposition, but the more interesting story here is the growing confidence behind women traveling independently while still wanting the social connection of a shared experience. Solo doesn’t have to mean solitary, and for travelers who have spent years coordinating everyone else’s schedules, that may be the most appealing luxury of all.

Photo credit: Illuminare Retreat

item.title: Virginia Takes Over Philadelphia to Turn Phillies Fans Into Fall Travelers
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Virginia is bringing its iconic Virginia is for Lovers brand back to Philadelphia this Labor Day weekend, transforming the home of the Phillies into an invitation to trade baseball season for a Virginia getaway. The 2026 “Philly Takeover” expands on last year’s campaign, with Virginia Tourism Corporation joined by seven destination partners — Charlottesville, Fairfax, Norfolk, Prince William, Richmond, Williamsburg and Virginia Beach — to put the Commonwealth in front of Philadelphia travelers throughout the fall.

The multi-channel campaign runs through October, with advertising spanning SEPTA’s NRG Station, Phillies broadcasts and digital channels, plus an in-stadium activation featuring a LOVEwork, fife and drum performers and destination giveaways. A Phillies Kiss Cam sponsorship, targeted social campaigns, radio spots, email marketing and a “Philly to VA” sweepstakes round out the effort, all designed to turn awareness into actual fall travel. With Philadelphia serving as a major drive market for Virginia, the campaign is strategically timed to capture travelers when thoughts naturally turn toward autumn escapes.

The Curated Take:
This is destination marketing with a decidedly different playbook. Rather than waiting for travelers to start searching for a fall getaway, Virginia is meeting them in one of Philadelphia’s biggest entertainment environments and borrowing the energy of baseball to sell the idea of a vacation. The timing is particularly smart: Virginia’s fall appeal stretches from mountain landscapes and wine country to historic towns, coastal destinations and vibrant cities, giving Phillies fans plenty of reasons to make the short trip south once the final pitch is thrown.

Photo credit: Virginia Tourism Corporation

item.title: Céline Dion’s Paris Comeback Could Turn Concert Nights Into a New Travel Boom
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Céline Dion’s return to the stage is poised to do more than bring fans back to the concert hall. Her 16-performance Paris residency, running September 12 through October 17, 2026, followed by 10 additional dates in May 2027, could create two distinct waves of visitor demand across the French capital. Luxury short-term rental platform Veeve points to previous major events as evidence of how dramatically cultural moments can reshape Paris’s accommodation market.

Veeve recorded a 40% year-over-year increase in Paris bookings during Taylor Swift’s 2024 Eras Tour, while nights booked nearly doubled, rising 93%. The 2024 Olympic Games generated an even larger effect, with bookings up 49%, nights booked up 86% and host booking revenue climbing 126%. With Dion’s residency spread across two seasons, Veeve sees another opportunity for homeowners to open their properties to visitors and for travelers, particularly families and groups, to choose professionally managed homes over traditional hotels.

The Curated Take:
Paris has always been a destination in its own right, but major cultural events have a way of changing when people visit and how long they stay. Céline Dion’s return gives fans another reason to build a Paris trip around a specific moment, potentially turning a concert into a longer French getaway. And with the residency returning in May 2027, this isn’t just a single burst of demand. It could create two very different opportunities to experience Paris through the lens of one of music’s most anticipated comebacks.

Photo credit: Veeve / UnderTheDoormat Group

item.title: The Olympic Flame’s Historic Journey to Dakar Begins
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
For the first time in Olympic history, the Youth Olympic flame will illuminate Africa as it makes its way from Athens to Dakar ahead of the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games. Lit by the sun’s rays in the historic Panathenaic Stadium on September 10, the flame will arrive in Senegal on September 12, launching a 30-stop journey through all 14 regions of the country before returning to Dakar for the Games’ October 31 opening ceremony.

More than a ceremonial relay, the Dakar 2026 Flame Tour is being positioned as a celebration of Senegalese culture, youth and the Olympic values of excellence, friendship and respect. Under the theme “Pass the Energy,” the tour will showcase the country’s spirit of teranga, or hospitality and generosity, while connecting communities through sport and cultural programming. The arrival in Dakar will include the “March of the Linguères,” a procession of 100 Senegalese women, cultural performances and a public celebration at Place du Souvenir. Across Africa, more than 40 National Olympic Committees and Olymafrica centers will also participate in a symbolic 30,500-kilometer relay representing the approximate perimeter of the continent.

The Curated Take:
This is bigger than a flame relay. Dakar 2026 represents a genuine milestone: the first Olympic sporting event to take place on African soil. The journey of the flame turns that milestone into something travelers can experience through the people, places and culture of Senegal, long before the athletes arrive. For travelers interested in seeing Senegal at a particularly significant moment, the weeks leading up to the Games offer a fascinating window into a country preparing to welcome the world.

item.title: Riviera Travel Opens 2028 Worldwide Collection with New Long-Haul Destinations
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Riviera Travel has released its 2028 Worldwide Collection earlier than ever, anchored by three brand-new, expert-guided itineraries: a 16-day deep dive into Patagonia and Tierra del Fuego, a 15-day island-hopping journey through Indonesia’s temples and volcanic landscapes, and a comprehensive tour of French Canada paired with Niagara Falls. The early launch directly addresses growing market research showing that while modern travelers increasingly crave deep, authentic cultural immersion, they strongly prefer having structured local guidance to navigate unfamiliar customs and complex logistics. Beyond the three headline additions, the operator has also expanded its dedicated solo travel portfolio with specialized versions of its popular China, Silk Road, and Southern Africa itineraries.

The Curated Take

Releasing a 2028 long-haul program years in advance reflects a growing industry trend: experienced travelers are securing complex, bucket-list itineraries earlier than ever. By pairing remote expedition destinations like Patagonia and Komodo National Park with the safety net of an escorted tour and built-in cultural guidance, Riviera Travel addresses a key market sweet spot—delivering deep, immersive cultural exploration without the logistical friction of traveling entirely on your own.

item.title: Sweden is Building a Floating Soundwave to House Its First National Music Museum
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Sweden is finally giving its staggering global music legacy a dedicated national home, with the Swedish National Music Museum set to open in the coastal town of Västervik in July 2027. Despite consistently ranking among the world’s top three exporters of music, the country has never had a single national hub to chronicle its journey from local community arts programs to global chart domination. Designed by architecture firm OKIDOKI, the two-story, 8,600-square-foot floating structure will anchor in the Baltic Sea next to the historic Stegeholm castle ruins. Its exterior is designed to look like a “frozen soundwave” made of pulsating timber panels that mirror audio rhythms.

Choosing Västervik over Stockholm brings the museum directly to the roots of the “Swedish Music Miracle.” Spearheaded in part by ABBA legend and Västervik native Björn Ulvaeus—who owns the neighboring sustainable Slottsholmen resort—the museum lands right in the heart of Sweden’s historic folk music capital. Located about 174 miles south of Stockholm, the floating museum will break down how a small nation produced global hits from ABBA to Max Martin, alongside tech titans like Spotify. Visitors can immerse themselves in interactive exhibits before stepping outside to explore the surrounding 5,000-island Tjust Archipelago.

The Curated Take

For decades, Sweden has quietly written the soundtrack to American pop radio, yet its music history has remained scattered across individual band museums and local legends. By building a dedicated national monument over the Baltic Sea, Sweden is framing its music culture not as a series of lucky pop hits, but as a deliberate, national art form. The fact that you can tour state-of-the-art interactive exhibits on a floating architectural soundwave, step out onto the deck, and hop a ferry straight into a 5,000-island archipelago turns a simple museum visit into one of the most compelling cultural road trips in Europe.

item.title: Sundance Mountain Resort Expands Terrain with New High-Speed Quad and Ridgeline Run for 2026/2027 Season
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Sundance Mountain Resort is expanding its winter footprint with the addition of over 100 acres of new terrain, marked by a high-speed quad lift named Electric Horseman and a signature 1.7-mile groomed ridge run named Storyteller. This milestone marks the completion of the resort’s first phase of back mountain expansion, bringing its total skiable area to 605 acres while setting the stage for future expert terrain growth. Servicing over 1,850 vertical feet in just six minutes, Electric Horseman significantly boosts uphill capacity and provides direct access across the back mountain.

Carved out of the former Far East Ridgeline, the new Storyteller run delivers an upper-intermediate grooming experience complete with mountain vistas, while also providing advanced skiers access to three new tree-lined gladed chutes. The expansion honors the creative heritage and vision of founder Robert Redford, building upon a series of recent multi-year capital improvements—including the Outlaw Express Lift, expanded snowmaking systems, and the new Mountain Camp Day Lodge.

The Curated Take

Sundance has long been cherished for its intimate, art-infused sanctuary feel, but limited terrain and older lift infrastructure sometimes meant sacrificing lap counts for ambiance. This major back-mountain expansion strikes a ideal balance: by adding a high-speed quad that slashes transit times to six minutes and opening up 100+ acres of ridgeline and tree runs, the resort elevates its technical ski offering without losing the boutique, soul-driven identity that sets it apart from Utah’s mega-resorts.

item.title: Nuju Uluwatu Opens in Bali, Joining Preferred Hotels & Resorts’ Exclusive L.V.X. Collection
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
A new sanctuary has arrived on Bali’s southern peninsula with the official opening of Nuju Uluwatu, an adults-only resort now inducted into Preferred Hotels & Resorts’ prestigious L.V.X. Collection. Derived from the Indonesian word meaning “towards,” Nuju celebrates the vast architectural and artistic diversity of the entire Indonesian archipelago rather than limiting itself to traditional Balinese aesthetics. Designed around traditional home forms with layered rooflines and tropical gardens, the property’s accommodations range from One-Bedroom Pool Suites paying homage to Western Indonesia with rich green tones and handcrafted batik, to Cabanas and Signature Residences reflecting Eastern Indonesia through blue hues and hand-woven Flores textiles.

The wellness-focused resort weaves traditional culture into every facet of the guest experience, offering immersive batik painting workshops, classical storytelling, and regional dance alongside a full spa, sauna, cold plunge pools, and modern fitness spaces. At the center of the resort sits Sana, an open-concept venue serving Modern Australian cuisine inflected with bold Asian flavors, spanning an indoor dining room, lounge, and poolside garden.

The Curated Take

Uluwatu’s clifftop hotel scene can often skew toward slick, generic modernism, but Nuju stands out by grounding its design in authentic Indonesian heritage. By drawing architectural elements, textile traditions, and artistic craftsmanship from islands across the entire archipelago—and reserving the sanctuary strictly for adults—the resort delivers a deeply serene, culturally rich escape that feels far more soulful than typical luxury openings.

item.title: Atlanta Beltline Reaches Historic 17-Mile Milestone Ahead of 2026 World Cup
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Beltline celebrated a landmark 20th-anniversary milestone with the official opening of Southside Trail Segments 2 + 3, creating an uninterrupted 16.7-mile continuous loop known as “The U.” The newly opened 1.9-mile stretch links Pittsburgh Yards to Boulevard, bridging the Eastside and Westside trails and reconnecting 36 historic Atlanta neighborhoods across the Northwest, Westside, Southside, Eastside, and Northeast sectors. Backed by over $31 million in federal and regional funding, the accelerated project delivers crucial transit infrastructure just in time for the city to host eight FIFA World Cup 2026™ matches.

First envisioned in 1999 as a 22-mile urban loop along historic freight rail lines, the Beltline has grown into one of the country’s most ambitious redevelopment initiatives. The project functions as the world’s longest linear arboretum in partnership with Trees Atlanta, serves as the city’s largest outdoor arts destination, and has spurred over $14 billion in private investment. With 16.7 miles of mainline trail and 10.3 miles of connector paths now open, the project remains on track to complete the final 4.7 miles of the full 22-mile loop by 2030.

The Curated Take

The completion of “The U” transforms what was once a series of disconnected neighborhood path segments into a truly unified urban transport artery. By linking historic Southside neighborhoods to existing Eastside and Westside hubs ahead of the global spotlight of the 2026 World Cup, Atlanta demonstrates how infrastructure-led multi-use paths can redefine urban mobility, drive equitable economic development, and establish a new benchmark for linear green spaces worldwide.

Photo Credit Atlanta Beltline, Inc. Photo by Erin Sintos
